subject: Re: Ledgerly — SLA-sensitive tiling and concurrency probe

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aarav Mehta <aarav@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T15:04:00Z
Subject: Ledgerly — SLA-sensitive tiling and concurrency probe

Hi Aarav —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. To make sure our Dedicated sizing is aligned with Ledgerly’s mixed workload (low-latency chat + heavy offline embedding pipelines + nightly index rebuilds), can you confirm a few quick items and attach a small sample of request logs if available? I outlined the key dimensions below so we can generate a provisional fleet sketch:

- Primary workload types (select all that apply): interactive chat (RAG), batch embedding refreshes, synchronous API for summaries, reranking.
- Target p95 latency for interactive requests (ms).
- Typical prompt token length (min/median/max) and typical response token length (min/median/max).
- Peak concurrent interactive sessions (API connections) vs sustained concurrency over a 1h window.
- QPS profile: baseline QPS and peak QPS (15m rolling).
- Dayparting: hours of weekday peak, weekend behavior, nightly batch windows.
- KV-cache hit ratio expectations (if you have session affinity).
- Percentage of calls that rely on embeddings / semantic search per interactive request.

If you can attach a 24–72h anonymized sample CSV (timestamp, model_type, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, user_id_hash) that would be ideal — even 1–2k rows helps. I’m including Marissa on the thread; she’s going to map this to possible GPU mixes and quantization options.

Attachments: sample CSV template (see link)

Next steps: once we have the sample I’ll run it through a quick estimator and send back a provisional allocation (GPU SKUs, headroom, and a recommended burst policy).

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Aarav Mehta <aarav@ledgerly.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Park <nina.park@ledgerly.com>, ops@ledgerly.com
Date: 2026-12-03T09:26:00Z
Subject: Re: Ledgerly — SLA-sensitive tiling and concurrency probe

Karthik —

Thanks. Quick answers inline, and I attached a 48h sample (ledgerly-traffic-sample.csv) — anonymized user IDs, removed PII. High level:

- Workloads: interactive chat (RAG-backed, majority of user-facing traffic), async daily/weekly embedding refresh jobs for our similarity index, scheduled nightly batch summarization reports for enterprise customers, occasional heavy reranking for search verticals.
- Target p95 latency: interactive chat (RAG): 120–150 ms p95; non-interactive sync APIs: 300–600 ms acceptable.
- Prompt tokens (min/median/max): 18 / 240 / 1,200 (longest are uploaded docs truncated by client); response tokens (min/median/max): 6 / 220 / 900. Median prompt+response ~460 tokens.
- Peak concurrent interactive sessions: 1,200 connections at 10:00 PST peak weekday; sustained concurrency 450 over rolling 1h windows.
- QPS: baseline ~70 qps, 15m peak ~420 qps (burst windows typically 09:00–11:00 PST & 16:00–17:00 PST; weekends have a ~30% lower baseline but nightly rebuild spikes).
- Dayparting: primary business hours PST; daily night window 01:00–04:00 for embedding index rebuilds (these are batch, can be throttled).
- KV-cache: we expect a 28–35% meaningful KV-cache hit rate at session affinity today (we'd like to improve this).
- Embedding dependence: ~40% of interactive requests trigger a vector lookup (top-k retrieval) before model call; many calls then call a small chat model for answer generation.

Additional notes: our dataset contains a mix of short transactional prompts and long doc-based prompts; we’d like to keep the long-doc flows on a higher memory SKU and use quantized smaller models for quick transactional replies.

Attached: ledgerly-traffic-sample.csv (48h); ops@ledgerly.com included for scheduling a short workshop if needed.

—Aarav
CTO, Ledgerly
aarav@ledgerly.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aarav Mehta <aarav@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Ledgerly — SLA-sensitive tiling and concurrency probe

Aarav — really helpful, thanks for the sample and the quick breakdown. A few clarifying follow-ups so our provisional sketch matches operational constraints:

1) Long-doc flows: when you say prompts up to 1,200 tokens, are those single-shot calls or do you maintain longer context across session turns (i.e., KV cache reuse)? If the latter, provide an example session length and typical KV cache reuse rate.

2) For the 40% of interactive requests that trigger vector lookups: what’s the average top-k returned (k) and do you run re-ranking in a separate model pass or in the same generation call? This affects extra GPU cycles for rerankers.

3) Index rebuild concurrency: during the nightly rebuilds, how many parallel embedding workers do you run and what percent of cluster CPU/GPU do they consume today (rough estimate)? Can those be rate-limited to avoid interfering with morning peak ramp?

4) Do enterprise customers have hard p95 SLAs that would force dedicated overprovisioning, or are the SLAs soft (credits/alerts)?

Provisional path I’ll explore after your reply: a two-tier dedicated pool — a small high-memory set for long-doc RAG sessions (pinned to higher VRAM SKUs), plus a higher throughput quantized pool for transactional replies and batched embedding workers. We’ll also model prefix/KV caching effect on occupancy and suggest a burst policy that uses lower-priority preemptible capacity for index rebuilds.

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute sizing workshop — Marissa, can you propose 2 slots tomorrow?

Thanks —
Karthik

Karthik / Marissa / Aarav —

Appreciate the detail, Aarav. From a commercial/ops perspective, I’m comfortable moving forward with a provisional allocation so the deals team can include a recommended committed capacity in LDG-2026-058. Marissa — please produce a short provisional sizer (PDF) that includes:

- Two-tier pool suggestion (high-memory SKUs + quantized throughput SKUs)
- Minimum reserved capacity to meet 150 ms p95 under weekday peak with 20% headroom
- Burst policy that leverages preemptible instances for nightly rebuilds and a canary fallback plan for morning ramp
- Estimated monthly cost delta between keeping rebuilds on dedicated vs moving to a hybrid burst-offload approach

Aarav — we’ll keep the nightly rebuilds as a throttled background job in the first pass; if you can confirm parallel embedding worker count (or share ops-runbook link) we can refine the cost/impact numbers.

I attached a short provisional sketch (redwood-provisional-sizer.pdf) — Marissa, update and send to Aarav by EOD PST.

Laura Bennett
